extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, landowners, private sector, and Federal/State/Tribal/local governments who must respond to or comment on information collection requirements for experimental populations under the Endangered Species Act
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on ICR renewals for experimental populations
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare or submit public comments and implement reporting obligations for the Fish and Wildlife Service's Paperwork Reduction Act renewals of information collections (ICRs) related to experimental populations under 50 CFR 17.84 (including Colorado gray wolf and grizzly bear NEPs). The page lists required data elements, reporting timelines, authorization procedures, and topics the agency requests comment on.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA comment topic — necessity/practical utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether or not the information will have practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Service specifically requests public comment on whether the information collection is necessary and has practical utility; responses will be included or summarized in the ICR submitted to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA comment topic — accuracy of burden estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of our estimate of the burden for this collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address whether the stated respondent counts, response frequencies, completion times, and total burden hours are accurate and whether the methodology/assumptions used to compute them are valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA comment topic — quality, utility, and clarity of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency requests suggestions to improve what is collected and how questions/requirements are phrased so that responses are more useful and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA comment topic — minimizing respondent burden
rubrics_metrics.description: How might the agency minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include permitting electronic submission of response; commenters should propose feasible burden-reduction measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of information collected — General take or removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations at 50 CFR 17.84 identify 'General take or removal' as a category of information collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'take' per the ESA: 'harass, harm, pursue, hunt, shoot, wound, kill, trap, capture, or collect, or to attempt to engage in any such conduct.' Examples of take include unintentional taking incidental to lawful activities (e.g., highway mortalities), animal husbandry actions (translocation or aiding sick/injured/orphaned individuals), take in defense of human life, take related to defense of property (if authorized), or authorized harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of information collected — Depredation-related take
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about take for management purposes of documented livestock depredation, which may include authorized harassment or authorized lethal take of experimental population animals in the act of attacking livestock (see 50 CFR 17.84).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Service collects depredation incident reports to assess effectiveness of control activities and to develop means to reduce problems with livestock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of information collected — Specimen collection / recovery / reporting dead individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Information documenting incidental or authorized scientific collection, reporting of sightings, or inadvertent discovery of injured or dead individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimens must be retained or disposed of only in accordance with directions from the Service; this category helps monitor reintroduction success and mortality causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data elements for incident reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The information that we collect includes: (a) Name, address, and phone number of reporting party; (b) Species involved; (c) Type of incident; (d) Quantity of take; (e) Location and time of the reported incident; and (f) Description of the circumstances related to the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six fields are standard information collected by telephone or email contacts and are used across the listed ICRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondents / Affected public and respondent's obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents include individuals and households, private sector, and State/local/Tribal governments (varies by ICR). Respondent's obligation is listed as either 'Voluntary' or 'Required to obtain or retain a benefit' depending on the specific ICR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice specifies respondent categories for each collection (general experimental populations, Colorado gray wolf NEP, grizzly bear NEP) and whether responses are voluntary or required to obtain/retain a benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion times and burden-hour estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice lists estimated completion times per response (commonly 30 minutes) and total annual burden hours and respondent counts for each requirement (tables provided per ICR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables give per-requirement estimated respondents, responses, completion time, and total annual burden hours (e.g., many items listed as 30 min reporting and 30 min recordkeeping). Commenters may address the accuracy of these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of designated agent (Colorado gray wolf)
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated agent is an employee of a Federal, State, or Tribal agency authorized by the Service to conduct gray wolf management. A prospective designated agent submits a letter requesting designated agent status that includes a proposal for work, a list of individuals who may perform the work, and a resume (or similar) demonstrating qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Service responds with a letter authorizing designated agent status; this ICR requires reporting/recordkeeping time for appointment and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for written take authorization (gray wolf)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving confirmation of wolf activity on private land, a public land grazing allotment, or on a Tribal reservation, the Service or a designated agent may issue written take authorization valid for not longer than 1 year, with appropriate conditions, to intentionally harass wolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harassment must occur in the area and under the conditions as specifically identified in the written take authorization; reporting/recordkeeping time is estimated per request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for 'repeatedly depredating wolf or wolves' written take authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service or designated agent may issue a 'repeatedly depredating wolf or wolves' written take authorization of limited duration (45 days or fewer) to a landowner, their employees, or a public land grazing permittee to take up to a specified number of wolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization is limited in duration and scope; reporting/recordkeeping burdens are estimated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for gray wolf takes (timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise specified, any take of a gray wolf must be reported as follows: (a) Lethal take must be reported within 24 hours (additional reasonable time allowed if access limited); (b) Opportunistic or intentional harassment must be reported within 7 days; (c) Gray wolves taken into captivity for care or to be euthanized must be reported within 24 hours or as soon as reasonably appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reporting timelines are required unless otherwise specified in the rule or authorization; designated agents and authorities have corresponding responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report requirements (Colorado gray wolf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife must summarize monitoring information in an annual report due by June 30 each year while the gray wolf is federally listed during any portion of a calendar or biological year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual report includes, but is not limited to: (a) post-release wolf movements and behavior; (b) wolf minimum counts or abundance estimates; (c) reproductive success and recruitment; (d) territory use and distribution; (e) cause-specific wolf mortalities; and (f) a summary of wolf conflicts and associated management activities to minimize wolf conflict risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal requirements for take of gray wolves on Tribal lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribes seeking an exception to allow take of gray wolves impacting ungulate populations must develop a science-based proposal that at minimum includes: basis of ungulate management objectives; data showing herd below objectives; data showing wolves are a major cause; why removal is warranted; level/duration of removal proposed; how ungulate response will be measured and actions adjusted; demonstration attempts to address other causes and Tribal commitment to implement remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal must be subjected to both public and peer review prior to finalization; at least three independent peer reviewers with relevant expertise not staff of the submitting Tribe must review the proposal. The Service will evaluate and provide a written determination on whether actions are scientifically based and warranted before authorizing wolf removals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grizzly bear reporting requirements and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting parties must notify the Service when incidents occur and annually report number of grizzly bears relocated and removed. Standard information includes name/address/phone, species, type of incident, quantity of take, location/time, and description. Specific timelines: (i) lethal take must be reported by individuals within 24 hours to the Service's Ecological Services point of contact (authorized agencies follow MOU instructions); (ii) nonlethal take that results in injury by an individual must be reported within 5 days (authorities follow MOU timelines); (iii) recovery/reporting of dead individuals and specimen collection protocols apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incidental take from indirect activities (e.g., habitat modification causing harm) does not need to be reported; reporting methods are telephone or email to specified Service offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) for grizzly bear management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service will enter into MOUs with Federal, State, or Tribal agencies to authorize grizzly bear management consistent with the final rule; the Service does not expect MOUs with local governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service will collect information from relevant agencies in relation to these MOUs, typically about relocation and removal actions (see next rubric items).

rubrics_metrics.name: MOU actions — relocation of bears (grizzly)
rubrics_metrics.description: With prior approval from the Service, an authorized Federal, State, or Tribal authority may live-capture any grizzly bear occurring in the NEP area and transport and release it in a remote location agreed to by the Service, State wildlife agency, and applicable land-managing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relocation requires prior Service approval and coordination with specified agencies; reporting and recordkeeping burden estimates apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOU actions — removal of grizzly bears involved in conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized Service, Federal, State, or Tribal authorities may lethally take a grizzly bear in the NEP area with prior approval from the Service if it is not reasonably possible to eliminate the threat by nonlethal deterrence or live-capturing and releasing the bear unharmed, and if the taking is done in a humane manner. Grizzly bears may be taken in self-defense or defense of others based on a good-faith belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal actions by authorized agencies follow MOU procedures and must be reported as specified in the final rule or MOU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written authorization — conditioned lethal take (grizzly)
rubrics_metrics.description: With prior written agreement from the Service, individuals may lethally take a grizzly bear within 200 yards (183 meters) of legally present livestock in Management Areas B and C if a depredation has been confirmed by the Service or an authorized agency and it has been determined nonlethal deterrence or live-capture is not reasonably possible. The Service may also authorize killing in Management Area C for an ongoing threat to human safety, livestock, or other property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization is conditioned on confirmation of depredation or identification of an ongoing threat and prior written agreement; reporting/recordkeeping burdens apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining landowner / land management entity authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals requesting written authorizations (e.g., for lethal take) must also obtain or confirm authorization from the landowner or land management entity, where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stated prerequisite for certain authorizations and part of the information/authorization process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collected information — management and recovery evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service will use collected information to assess effectiveness of control activities, determine causes of mortality and conflicts, document locations of reintroduced animals, and evaluate success of reintroductions in relation to established recovery plan goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information helps Service recovery specialists and managers to minimize conflicts, improve management techniques, and support OMB ICR justification.
